bar.signalroutes.tooltip: Signal routes: the routes of the rail signals and the track each one clears. Click a route to show it on the map.
sigroute.empty: This map has no signal routes.
sigroute.empty.hint: Signal routes (signalroutes.cfg) tell trains and trams which track a signal clears. Maps without rail signals do not need them.
sigroute.summary: {count, plural, one {# route} other {# routes}} at {signals, plural, one {# signal} other {# signals}}
sigroute.file_problems: signalroutes.cfg has {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}} that belong to no route. Hover for details.
sigroute.filter.tooltip: Showing only the routes of this signal. Click to show all routes.
sigroute.row.tooltip: Show this route on the map: its track pieces and signals.
sigroute.row.pieces: {count, plural, one {# track piece} other {# track pieces}}
sigroute.detail.track: {found, number} of {count, number} track pieces found on the map
sigroute.status.selected: Route {number}: {count, plural, one {# track piece} other {# track pieces}}, {found, number} found on the map.
sigroute.status.failed: Could not read the signal routes: {reason}
sigroute.edited.tooltip: This route differs from the original map.
sigroute.edit.kind.tooltip: The kind number of the route, a whole number from 0.
sigroute.edit.aspect.tooltip: What the signal shows when this route is set. A speed limit sets reduced speed, no limit sets proceed.
sigroute.edit.aspect.other: Aspect {aspect} comes from another map or program. It stays as it is until you choose one of these.
sigroute.edit.distant.tooltip: The ID of the signal that announces this route. Leave empty for none.
sigroute.edit.next.tooltip: The ID of the signal that follows this route. Leave empty for none.
sigroute.edit.speed.tooltip: The speed limit of the route in km/h. Leave empty for no limit.
sigroute.edit.remove.tooltip: Take this signal out of the route.
sigroute.edit.pick.tooltip: Click a signal on the map to use its ID. Esc stops.
sigroute.edit.delete.tooltip: Take this route out of signalroutes.cfg. Undo brings it back.
sigroute.delete.title: Delete route {number}?
sigroute.delete.text: The route is taken out of signalroutes.cfg. Its track pieces and signals can be deleted afterwards. Undo brings the route back.
sigroute.status.pick_distant: Click a signal on the map to make it the distant signal of route {number}. Esc stops.
sigroute.status.pick_next: Click a signal on the map to make it the next signal of route {number}. Esc stops.
sigroute.status.pick_ended: Picking stopped. The route stays as it is.
sigroute.status.edited: Route {number} changed. Undo takes it back.
sigroute.status.deleted: Route {number} deleted. Undo brings it back.
sigroute.status.bad_kind: The kind is a whole number, 0 or more.
sigroute.status.bad_id: Enter the ID of a signal on the map, or leave the field empty.
sigroute.status.bad_speed: Enter a speed in km/h above 0, or leave the field empty for no limit.
sigroute.new.tooltip: Plan a new route. Choose the signal, look at the ways over the track and create the route.
sigroute.new.title: New signal route
sigroute.new.signal.pick.tooltip: Click the signal of the new route on the map. Esc stops.
sigroute.new.target.next.tooltip: The route ends at the next signal ahead that has a route of its own.
sigroute.new.target.signal.tooltip: The route ends at the piece of track beside a signal you choose.
sigroute.new.target.track.tooltip: The route ends with a piece of track you choose.
sigroute.new.target.pick.tooltip: Click the target on the map, a signal or a piece of track. Esc stops.
sigroute.new.start.auto.tooltip: Start where OMSI's own routes do. At the signal's piece of track when the signal stands in its first half, else at the next piece.
sigroute.new.start.at.tooltip: The route starts with the piece of track the signal stands beside.
sigroute.new.start.after.tooltip: The route starts with the piece after the one the signal stands beside.
sigroute.new.start.note_at: The route starts at the piece of track beside the signal.
sigroute.new.start.note_after: The route starts at the piece after the one beside the signal.
sigroute.new.overlap.tooltip: How many track pieces the route runs on beyond the target signal, as a margin for trains that stop late. OMSI's own routes often run one piece on. Not for a chosen track piece.
sigroute.new.way: Way {number} ({length, number} m, {count, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}})
sigroute.new.way.overlap: Way {number} ({length, number} m, {count, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}} + {overlap, plural, one {# overlap} other {# overlap}})
sigroute.new.way.tooltip: Show this way on the map and use it for the route.
sigroute.new.ways.more: There are more ways than these. The shortest are listed.
sigroute.new.hint.signal: Click the signal of the new route on the map, or use the pipette.
sigroute.new.hint.target: Choose where the route ends: click a signal or a piece of track on the map.
sigroute.new.problem.no_track_at_signal: No rail runs beside signal {id} in the way it faces, within {meters} m. Choose a signal that stands beside its track.
sigroute.new.problem.unknown_target: The target is not on the map.
sigroute.new.problem.target_no_track: The target has no rail. A target signal needs track beside it, and a track piece must be a rail.
sigroute.new.problem.no_way: No rail leads from the signal to the target in the way the signal faces. A gap in the track, a target behind the signal or track that does not connect can be the reason.
sigroute.new.problem.too_far: No way up to {length} m and {pieces} track pieces. Choose a nearer target.
sigroute.new.problem.step_limit: The search gave up after looking at a very large number of track pieces. Choose a nearer target.
sigroute.new.problem.no_installation: Finding the track needs the object and spline files of the OMSI installation, and they were not found.
sigroute.new.aspect.auto.tooltip: A speed limit gives proceed at reduced speed, no limit gives proceed.
sigroute.new.distant.tooltip: The ID of the signal that announces this route. Filled in when the signal is its own distant signal on its other routes. Leave empty for none.
sigroute.new.next.tooltip: The ID of the signal that follows this route. Filled in with the signal the way ends at. Leave empty for none.
sigroute.new.create.tooltip: Write the route into signalroutes.cfg. Undo takes it back.
sigroute.new.status.no_installation: New signal routes need the object and spline files of the OMSI installation to find the track.
sigroute.new.status.cancelled: New route cancelled. Nothing was written.
sigroute.new.status.found: {count, plural, one {# way found} other {# ways found}}, the shortest is {length, number} m long.
sigroute.new.status.pick_signal: Click the signal of the new route on the map. Esc stops.
sigroute.new.status.pick_target: Click the end of the route on the map, a signal or a piece of track. Esc stops.
sigroute.new.status.pick_distant: Click a signal on the map to make it the distant signal of the new route. Esc stops.
sigroute.new.status.pick_next: Click a signal on the map to make it the next signal of the new route. Esc stops.
sigroute.new.status.pick_ended: Picking stopped. The plan stays as it is.
sigroute.new.status.no_signal_there: No signal at that spot. Click closer to a signal, or press Esc.
sigroute.new.status.no_target_there: No signal or track at that spot. Click closer, or press Esc.
sigroute.new.status.signals_reading: The signals of the map are still being read. Try again in a moment.
sigroute.new.status.rails_reading: The track is still being read. Try again in a moment.
sigroute.new.status.stale: The map changed since the ways were found. They are found again. Look at them, then press Create route.
sigroute.new.status.created: Route {number} created. Undo takes it back.
